title: Stateful environments for vertical agents — Josh Purtell, Synth Labs
talk_summary: Josh Purtell argues that vertical agents should manipulate a stateful environment — a separate process that owns the domain state and exposes a simplified representation to the agent — rather than embedding domain logic in the agent. The main payoffs he cites are model-swappability, multi-agent concurrency across network boundaries, and cheap reset/rollback enabling tree-search-style recovery from derailment.

takeaways.technique: Separate stateful environment process from agent logic
takeaways.what_they_do: Containerize the vertical app's logic and state in a process that never changes, with the agent only observing/manipulating a simplified representation over a network boundary.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you containerize the logic of your vertical app into code that never changes, it's a lot easier to completely revamp your agent when the new model comes out

takeaways.technique: Network-boundary isolation for async multi-agent work
takeaways.what_they_do: Run the environment as a separate process with standard network boundaries so multiple agents/models can work on the same product concurrently and asynchronously.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the answer to that question of how to do asynchronous work in a reliable way in production is network boundaries

takeaways.technique: Resettable environment / rollback for derailed runs
takeaways.what_they_do: Because state lives outside the agent, you can snapshot, reset, and roll back the artifact the agent is working on when it derails, instead of restarting the whole run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a lot of people working with agents in a in a code setting know how valuable it is to just be able to roll back the agent after it's kind of gotten derailed

takeaways.technique: Tree-search over branches when a reset is cheap
takeaways.what_they_do: With a resettable environment you get language-agent tree search almost for free: branch the agent in two directions, keep the better branch, discard the rest.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you have a resetable environment, you sort of get language agent tree search for free

takeaways.technique: Expose only the representation the agent needs
takeaways.what_they_do: Don't show the agent the whole OS/Excel app; expose a minimal, agent-legible view of just what it needs to observe and manipulate.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't have to show the agent the whole um OS you you kind of just show it what it needs to see in the terminal
